bull_bear.body: Priority 1: Fund real estate construction (internal accruals + cash reserves). Priority 2: Scale broking tech/platform. Priority 3: Run-off NBFC book to generate cash. No dividends mentioned; focus on reinvestment for growth. Net cash position (INR 750 Cr) provides buffer.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution risk on delivering 3x profit growth by FY28. Real estate cycle downturn affecting sales velocity. Delay in Worli tower leasing/commissioning. Regulatory changes in broking/ARC sectors. Concentration risk in NCR/Mumbai markets.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, transparent on past failures (fintech exit), and focused on 'execution' over 'vision'. Emphasized clean balance sheet, zero litigation, and predictable earnings visibility from signed pipelines.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The INR 3,000 Cr tax shield inherited from the merger creates a unique scenario where PBT equals PAT for the foreseeable future, artificially inflating net margins compared to peers. The NBFC book is being run off without debt, turning a traditional leveraged business into a pure cash-flow generator.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Stated policy is growth without leverage: zero net debt, with owned land parcels and JVs carrying no borrowings.
- ₹1,000.07 Cr preferential capital raise approved to fund GDV expansion entirely through equity rather than debt.
- Promoters are committing ₹709 Cr, roughly 71% of the raise, which will lift promoter holding from the current 33%.
- Shareholding stands at 33% promoters, 17.19% FII and DII, and 50% public and others; capital is deployed based on GDV and business-expansion opportunities.
- IARCL is substantially unlevered with 99.52% capital adequacy against the 15% RBI regulatory minimum and ₹520.15 Cr net worth.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- resource: a large development pipeline of owned and JV land — evidence: development portfolio of about 110.52 lakh sq. ft. of saleable area as on March 31, 2026, spanning launched, ongoing and future developments, with planned FY2027 launches of 39.74 lakh sq. ft. — against it: the portfolio is concentrated in the National Capital Region (86% of sq. ft.)
- integration: in-house recovery capability in asset reconstruction — evidence: IBARCL runs an integrated in-house recovery set-up including a ground collection team of approximately 2,200 members
- distribution: physical broking network behind the digital platform — evidence: presence across 14 cities with 174 associated partners and 200 dedicated relationship managers, serving over 9 lakh broking clients through 1.73 lakh demat accounts
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Credit and delinquency risk in lending portfolios — The company lists credit risk among its key exposures and relies on analytics to spot emerging delinquency patterns across customer segments and to step in early. Loan quality in the group's lending book, including Dhani Loans and Services, therefore depends on this monitoring.
- Liquidity, interest-rate and asset-liability risk — The company names liquidity and interest-rate risk and has them overseen by the ALCO and the Risk Management Committee. It says asset-liability comfort depends on the short-term maturity of its loan portfolio and on keeping adequate liquidity buffers while avoiding excessive leverage.
- Regulatory risk across RBI- and SEBI-regulated entities — The NBFC subsidiary Dhani Loans and Services must meet RBI prudential norms on asset classification, provisioning, capital adequacy and credit rating, and the group must comply with SEBI Listing Regulations. Any change or lapse directly affects the regulated businesses.
- Cyber security and data-privacy risk — The company treats customer data as a critical asset exposed to evolving cyber threats. It runs an ISO 27001-based ISMS and has started aligning its processes with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, a new compliance requirement.
- Geographic concentration of the real estate portfolio — The development portfolio is primarily concentrated in the National Capital Region. Now that real estate is the principal business, NCR market conditions drive most of the pipeline.
- Capital-market activity cyclicality in broking — The company disclosed that industry trading activity moderated and market activity stayed subdued for much of FY26. This leaves the broking business exposed to market volumes.
- Operational and business risk from the group restructuring — Operational and business risks are part of the stated risk universe. The group only emerged from a multi-entity Scheme of Arrangement during FY2025-26, and FY26 was its first full year of executing the renewed real estate strategy.

business.body:

latest_quarter.body: Real estate margins protected by 15% price appreciation post-launch and strict payment discipline (80% collection rate on sold units). Cost base streamlined via merger; no debt interest burden. Tax efficiency is a major margin driver (effective tax rate ~0% near term).

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Real estate profits expected to double in FY27 and triple in FY28 vs FY26 base; Margin: PBT = PAT until INR 3,000 Cr cumulative profit due to tax shield; Order Inflow: 40 Lakh sq ft launching in FY27 (GDV INR 6,000+ Cr); Capex/Commissioning: INR 600 Cr capex for Worli commercial tower, completion in 3-4 years.

outlook.body: Total GDV potential INR 21,000+ Cr across 1.1 Cr sq ft. Includes launched projects (75-100% sold: Estate Sector 104, Heights Sector 104), upcoming FY27 launches (40 Lakh sq ft, GDV INR 6,000+ Cr), and future pipeline (42 Lakh sq ft, GDV INR 11,900+ Cr). Mix of residential, commercial, and plotted developments in Gurugram, Mumbai, Ludhiana.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: 1) Commercial leasing annuity from Worli/Prabhadevi tower starting Year 4. 2) Re-rating of broking business with new online/algo stack capturing market share from incumbents. 3) Mark-to-market gains on US investment (SpringCash) as it scales disbursals. 4) Potential revival of NBFC lending post run-off (currently paused).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Make Real Estate the principal growth engine: build a scaled real estate platform through disciplined execution, strategic joint ventures and an asset-light development model.
- Strengthen Financial Services by expanding the digital broking franchise, growing the Asset Reconstruction platform and building technology-led financial solutions.
- Keep capital allocation disciplined and return-focused, with investment decisions guided by prudent leverage and defined return thresholds.
- Use technology and AI as differentiators across the Group, investing in digital platforms, automation and analytics (including for project planning, customer servicing, compliance and risk management).
- Simplify the corporate structure following the Scheme of Arrangement (merger of Dhani Services Limited and others into Indiabulls Limited, effective October 14, 2025) and focus management on the highest-value businesses.
- Real estate product focus on premium residential, mid-income residential and commercial developments in high-growth urban micro-markets, with phased monetisation.
- Transform Indiabulls Securities into a technology-driven digital discount broking platform.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Growth is mainly through real estate development rather than plant capacity. FY2025-26 was the first full year of the renewed real estate strategy: the company launched multiple residential developments across Gurugram and Kharkhoda. As on March 31, 2026 the development portfolio was an estimated 110.52 lakh sq. ft. of saleable area across launched, ongoing and future developments, mainly in the National Capital Region, delivered through owned developments and joint ventures. In financial services the build-out is platform-led: expanding digital trading platforms (mobile, web, desktop), enhancing the IB Algo retail algorithmic trading platform, strengthening UPI capability on the Dhani platform after NPCI approval as a Third Party Application Provider, and a continuing strategic investment in Spring Cash, a U.S.-based AI-enabled SMB financing platform. No project commissioning timelines appear in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Gurugram's share of Tier-I residential sales rose from 6.1% in CY21 to 14.6% in CY25, with average ticket size up 30% YoY in CY25 and units above ₹5 crore at 63% of revenue; management says its ₹2-6 crore ticket-size offerings are well positioned for this premium segment.
- Gurugram demand is underpinned by improving metro connectivity, proximity to IGI Airport and rising aspirations of high-income buyers along the Dwarka Expressway corridor.
- Revenue recognition from launched projects began in Q4FY26, and management cites strong earnings visibility over the medium term from phased monetisation of the pipeline.
- Long-term real estate demand from urbanisation, demographics, rising disposable incomes, infrastructure and government support for housing; the sector is expected to reach nearly US$1 trillion by 2030.
- Broking momentum improved in Q4 after industry trading activity moderated for much of FY26, which management attributes to investment in technology and customer acquisition.
- Asset reconstruction opportunity from the evolving regulatory framework, improving banking-sector asset quality and increasing institutional participation.
- Management says it remains mindful of macroeconomic uncertainties and changing market conditions going into FY2026-27.
- Development portfolio of approximately 110.52 lakh sq. ft. of saleable area with estimated GDV of over ₹21,366 crore as on March 31, 2026, spanning launched, ongoing and future developments (the CEO letter separately cites 112.2 lakh sq. ft. / over ₹23,608 crore across twelve projects).
- Projects launched in FY2026: 28.67 lakh sq. ft. of saleable area with sales potential of ₹3,393 crore.
- Planned launches for FY2027: 39.74 lakh sq. ft. with sales potential of ₹6,029 crore (four marquee projects).
- Next year and future pipeline: 42.11 lakh sq. ft. with sales potential of ₹11,944 crore.
- Portfolio mix: NCR 86% / Ludhiana 11% / Mumbai 2% of sq. ft.; residential 70%, commercial 15%, mixed development 12%, plotted land 3%.
- FY2025-26 sales bookings of ₹2,752 crore covering about 21.6 lakh sq. ft. across 909 units; collections of ₹400 crore.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Indiabulls has completed a 3-year restructuring to emerge as a net-cash entity with a clean balance sheet, pivoting aggressively back to its core real estate competency where a INR 21,000 Cr GDV pipeline promises a 3x PAT expansion by FY28. The removal of legacy litigations and loss-making fintech ventures unlocks significant value, supported by a unique tax shield that equates PBT to PAT for the next INR 3,000 Cr of profits.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Gurugram's share of Tier-I residential sales rose from 6.1% in CY21 to 14.6% in CY25, with average ticket size up 30% YoY in CY25 and units above ₹5 crore at 63% of revenue; management says its ₹2-6 crore ticket-size offerings are well positioned for this premium segment.
- Gurugram demand is underpinned by improving metro connectivity, proximity to IGI Airport and rising aspirations of high-income buyers along the Dwarka Expressway corridor.
- Revenue recognition from launched projects began in Q4FY26, and management cites strong earnings visibility over the medium term from phased monetisation of the pipeline.
- Long-term real estate demand from urbanisation, demographics, rising disposable incomes, infrastructure and government support for housing; the sector is expected to reach nearly US$1 trillion by 2030.
- Broking momentum improved in Q4 after industry trading activity moderated for much of FY26, which management attributes to investment in technology and customer acquisition.
- Asset reconstruction opportunity from the evolving regulatory framework, improving banking-sector asset quality and increasing institutional participation.
- Management says it remains mindful of macroeconomic uncertainties and changing market conditions going into FY2026-27.
- Development portfolio of approximately 110.52 lakh sq. ft. of saleable area with estimated GDV of over ₹21,366 crore as on March 31, 2026, spanning launched, ongoing and future developments (the CEO letter separately cites 112.2 lakh sq. ft. / over ₹23,608 crore across twelve projects).
- Projects launched in FY2026: 28.67 lakh sq. ft. of saleable area with sales potential of ₹3,393 crore.
- Planned launches for FY2027: 39.74 lakh sq. ft. with sales potential of ₹6,029 crore (four marquee projects).
- Next year and future pipeline: 42.11 lakh sq. ft. with sales potential of ₹11,944 crore.
- Portfolio mix: NCR 86% / Ludhiana 11% / Mumbai 2% of sq. ft.; residential 70%, commercial 15%, mixed development 12%, plotted land 3%.
- FY2025-26 sales bookings of ₹2,752 crore covering about 21.6 lakh sq. ft. across 909 units; collections of ₹400 crore.

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.
